blocks.content: Tribunals are quasi-judicial institutions established to provide speedy and specialized justice in specific areas such as administration, taxation, armed forces, company law, and environmental disputes. They reduce the burden on traditional courts and deliver expert-driven decisions.

items: Identify tribunals as quasi-judicial institutions rather than standard judicial courts.
Memorize the key specialized areas: administration, taxation, armed forces, company law, and environmental disputes.
Focus on the main twin objectives: providing speedy/specialized justice and reducing court backlog.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Tribunals are established as quasi-judicial bodies to resolve specialized disputes.
They cater to specific areas including administration, taxation, armed forces, company law, and environmental disputes.
Their core purpose is to deliver speedy and specialized justice while lessening the case burden on traditional courts.
Decisions rendered by tribunals are characterized by expert-driven insights.
